Look up Danish industry labels for DB07 or DB25 codes

Source: R/db_label.R
db_label.Rd

Returns the Danish titles from Statistics Denmark's bundled classification tables. Supports full six-digit industry codes, two-, three-, and four-digit hierarchy codes, and uppercase section letters such as "A". Dots and whitespace are removed automatically, including mixed input.

Usage

db_label(x, version)

Source

Statistics Denmark: DB25 and conversion tables, sheets 3. DB25 Alle koder and 4. DB07 Alle koder in the branch key. Source page updated 26 February 2026; downloaded 24 October 2026.

Arguments

x

A vector of industry codes, coerced to character if needed.

version

Required classification: "DB25" or "DB07".

Value

A character vector of Danish labels in the same order and with the same length as x.

Details

Always choose version = "DB07" or version = "DB25" explicitly. Identical codes can have different meanings in the two classifications. This function looks up labels, it does not convert between classifications. Unknown or malformed codes return NA with a warning. Missing input stays missing without a warning. Leading zeroes are never guessed, so keep codes as character data. No internet connection is needed.

See also

format_db07(), convert_db07_to_db25(), convert_db25_to_db07()

Examples

db_label(c("011200", "01.12.00", NA), version = "DB25")
#> [1] "Dyrkning af ris" "Dyrkning af ris" NA               
db_label("01.49.10", version = "DB07")
#> [1] "Kenneler"
db_label(c("A", "01", "01.1", "01.11"), version = "DB25")
#> [1] "LANDBRUG, JAGT, SKOVBRUG OG FISKERI"                              
#> [2] "Plante- og husdyravl, jagt og serviceydelser i forbindelse hermed"
#> [3] "Dyrkning af etårige afgrøder"                                     
#> [4] "Dyrkning af korn (undtagen ris), bælgfrugter og olieholdige frø"  
# df |> dplyr::mutate(branche_label = db_label(dbkode, version = "DB07"))
